English: Ritual Stand
A simple wooden dais, hastily erected on the steppe, for basic Zoroastrian prayers and gatherings. Marks the most basic center for communal worship.
Wicker Fence
A woven fence of local reeds and sticks encircles the worship area, protecting rituals from prying eyes and symbolically marking sacred ground.
Shrine Patch
A cleared and consecrated patch of earth, with stone markers and a permanent fire-pit, serves as a fixed point for communal rites and fire worship.
Priests Shelter
A sturdy felt tent or yurt for the mobed (priest) and sacred implements, allowing for more regular rituals and spiritual leadership among the clan.
Spirit Pavilion
A large, semi-permanent pavilion of felt and wood, appointed with sacred banners and fire altars, hosts larger clan gatherings and seasonal rituals.
Sanctified Room
A wooden or stone-walled chamber, kept ritually pure, where sacred fires burn protected from the wind. Marks a transition to more permanent and respected worship.
Blessed Chamber
A stone structure with an inner sanctum, reserved for fire priests and the most sacred rites. Clan leaders gather here to seek divine favor.
Diviners Hall
A grand hall decorated with sacred motifs, where priests interpret omens and guide the clans spiritual path. Becomes a center of unity and tradition.
Holy Room
A sanctified chamber with intricate carvings, dedicated to the holiest fires and used for the most significant clan ceremonies, drawing all in devotion.
Zoroastrian Ritual Hall
An awe-inspiring hall of stone and wood, adorned with fire altars, sacred texts, and relics. It anchors the faith of the clan and cements spiritual unity.
